q.intro.text: Main Street and Oak Avenue are both straight, and they cross. At one corner the angle between them is 65 degrees.

q.ask.text: What is the angle at the corner across the intersection?

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one: the picture moves first, then the notation.

e.s1.text: The streets become two lines, A C and B D, crossing at O. The only number we know: the measure of angle A O B equals 65 degrees.

e.s2.text: Angle A O B and angle B O C share the side O B, and their outer sides O A and O C are opposite rays of line A C. That makes them a linear pair: together they fill a straight angle, 180 degrees.

e.s3.text: So 65 plus x equals 180, and x equals 115. The angle at the next corner, the measure of angle B O C, is 115 degrees.

e.s4.text: Line B D gives a second linear pair: 115 plus the measure of angle C O D equals 180, so the measure of angle C O D equals 65 degrees. The angle across the crossing equals the one we started with.

e.why.text: Quick check: why do angle A O B and angle B O C add up to 180 degrees?

e.w-ok.text: Yes. The drawn line makes a straight angle, and the two angles fill it exactly.

e.w-adj.text: Being next to each other is not enough: adjacent angles can add up to anything. The drawn line is what makes 180 degrees.

e.w-look.text: Looks are not a reason. The reason is in the figure: line A C is drawn.

t.intro.text: Now lines P R and Q S cross at O, and the measure of angle P O Q equals 38 degrees. The first two steps are done for you.

t.pair.text: Angle P O Q and angle Q O R are a linear pair on line P R: they add up to 180 degrees.

t.x-ask.text: Write the equation, then type the measure of angle Q O R.

t.x-ok.text: Yes: 38 plus 142 equals 180, so the measure of angle Q O R equals 142 degrees.

t.x-swap.text: That uses 90. A straight angle is 180 degrees: 38 plus x equals 180.

t.x-equal.text: That copies the 38 degrees. These two angles sit side by side on a line: they add up to 180 degrees, they are not equal.

t.x-whole.text: 180 is the whole straight angle. Take away the 38 degrees you know.

t.x-other.text: Not quite. 38 plus x equals 180: what is x?

t.y-ask.text: Now go across the crossing. What is the measure of angle R O S?

t.y-ok.text: Yes: angle Q O R and angle R O S are a linear pair on line Q S, so 180 minus 142 equals 38. Vertical angles are equal, even when they open sideways.

t.y-supp.text: 142 degrees is the angle next to it. Use line Q S: 142 plus the measure of angle R O S equals 180.

t.y-swap.text: A straight angle is 180 degrees, not 90 degrees: 142 plus the measure of angle R O S equals 180.

t.done.text: The last corner, angle S O P, is 142 degrees: it is across from angle Q O R.

t.cb-right.text: You were right: 65 degrees. The angle across a crossing always equals the angle you start from, and now you can show why.

t.cb-supp.text: 115 degrees is the corner next door: those two are a linear pair. The corner across is 65 degrees.

t.cb-unknown.text: It had no number on it, but it could still be found: two linear pairs give 65 degrees.

t.cb-none.text: The corner across the intersection is 65 degrees.

p.intro.text: Jordan measured five crossings with a protractor. Every time, the angles across from each other were equal. Jordan says: That proves it for every crossing.

p.build.text: Right: five examples are not every crossing. Let’s build a proof that works for any two lines. Choose a reason for each statement.

p.build-test.text: Five checks cannot cover every crossing: there are endlessly many. Let’s build a proof that does. Choose a reason for each statement.

p.given.text: Given: lines A C and B D cross at O. Prove: the measure of angle 1 equals the measure of angle 3.

p.r1.text: The measure of angle 1 plus the measure of angle 2 equals 180 degrees

p.r2.text: The measure of angle 2 plus the measure of angle 3 equals 180 degrees

p.r3.text: The measure of angle 1 plus the measure of angle 2 equals the measure of angle 2 plus the measure of angle 3

p.r4.text: The measure of angle 1 equals the measure of angle 3

p.c1.text: Yes. Line A C is drawn, so angle 1 and angle 2 fill a straight angle.

p.c2.text: Yes. The same with line B D: angle 2 and angle 3 fill the other straight angle.

p.c3.text: Both sums are 180 degrees, so they are equal to each other.

p.c4.text: Take angle 2 away from both sides, and what is left is angle 1 equals angle 3.

p.x-measure.text: Measuring checks one crossing. A reason in a proof has to work for every crossing.

p.x-adj.text: Adjacent alone does not give 180 degrees. Which drawn line makes the straight angle?

p.x-other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different statement. Which reason makes this one true?

p.done.text: That’s a proof. It never used a measurement, so it works for every pair of crossing lines. Watch: whatever the crossing, angle 1 equals angle 3.
